verified.notes: Thompson Hine SmarTrade summary of U.S. Commerce Section 232 titanium-sponge report, fetched 200. Stored excerpt 'only one producer by 2019 capable of producing the product for defense, commercial and industrial applications' verbatim on page. The 68% import-reliance figure ALSO confirmed verbatim ('The United States imports 68 percent of the titanium sponge needed to fulfill domestic demand') — basis is U.S. sponge import reliance (national, not launch-specific), matching the node note. Both user-flagged claims confirmed. Grey-ish (legal-trade summary of a gov report, not the primary Commerce doc); appropriate for the near-single-source upstream framing, not a SpaceX claim.

Aviation Week (whitelist tier-1 supply-chain reporting), fetched 200. Stored excerpt verbatim: 'The aerospace castings sector, a roughly $10 billion industry, is dominated by two leading providers: Arconic and Precision Castparts (PCC).' User-flagged 'dominated by two leading providers' phrase confirmed exact. $10B is aerospace-castings sector size (not launch-specific), correctly labelled. Names Arconic+PCC as the two; Howmet is the engine-casting successor lineage to Arconic's castings business, as the limitations field notes — the edge to Howmet rests on a separate Howmet vendor source, not on this duopoly naming.

Constellium press release (company news, whitelist), fetched 200. Stored excerpt verbatim: 'Under this agreement, Constellium is to supply Airware® aluminium plates and sheets for Blue Origin's massive orbital rocket, New Glenn.' User-flagged New Glenn Al-Li supply link CONFIRMED. CAVEAT: this release says 'Airware® aluminium' and does NOT use the string 'aluminium-lithium / Al-Li' on the page; the Al-Li identity of Airware is established by the separate product page (ev_space_constellium_alli_product). The stored excerpt's quote contains no 'Al-Li' string, so the verbatim quote is clean; the Al-Li framing is in node prose, sourced elsewhere — acceptable. Confirms a reusable-launch-program supply link (Blue Origin New Glenn), not SpaceX.

Constellium space-market page (vendor_claim, whitelist-grey vendor marketing — valid for product-offered role), fetched 200. Stored excerpt verbatim incl. the slightly awkward original comma placement: 'We offer high-performance aluminum such, as aluminum-lithium alloys, in plate, sheet and extrusions for key structural components, including dome caps, barrel panels, stiffeners, intertanks, stage adapters / interstage structures, thrust structures, heat shields, and crew modules.' No numeric claim. Establishes Al-Li product for launch-vehicle structures; vendor page, does not prove a SpaceX/Falcon 9 BOM selection (limitations field correct).

Constellium Airware product page (vendor_claim), fetched 200. Stored excerpt verbatim: 'Airware®, Constellium's proprietary aluminum-lithium solution, delivers a breakthrough in material performance' (page continues '—offering significantly lower density, higher stiffness...'). This is the source that establishes Airware = aluminum-lithium, supporting the Al-Li framing used in the New Glenn record's node prose. No numeric claim; weak for share quantification, correctly not used for one.

Kaiser Aluminum FY2024 press release on GlobeNewswire (whitelist company release), fetched 200. Substance EXACT but one typographic difference: page reads 'a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products, serving customers worldwide with highly-engineered solutions for aerospace and high-strength, packaging...' whereas stored excerpt drops the comma after 'products' ('...specialty aluminum products serving customers...'). Meaning identical. Separately CONFIRMED the node-note $883M figure verbatim at correct basis: 'Net sales for aerospace/high strength applications were $883 million' (FY2024 aerospace/high-strength NET SALES, distinct from the $530M conversion revenue on the same line — basis correctly stated in node). Marked partial only on the comma drift; recommend trivially re-aligning excerpt comma to exact.

Light Metal Age trade press, fetched 200. Stored excerpt 'increase in heat treat plate production capacity by approximately 25%' verbatim on page. Node-note $375M figure ALSO confirmed verbatim ('The $375 million multi-year expansion and operational security investment project at its Trentwood facility'). 25% is a heat-treat-plate capacity-expansion figure (aero/GE plate, not launch-specific), correctly labelled. Trade press (whitelist-acceptable for capacity disclosure echo).

Resolved via the ARCONIC PRIMARY 8-K exhibit on SEC EDGAR (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1790982/000115752323000718/a53393351ex99_1.htm; curl HTTP 200, 21315B intact). Stored excerpt ('Shares of Arconic Corp., based in Pittsburgh, will no longer trade on the New York Stock Exchange once the transaction closes') is the AP/WQAD rewording of this same fact — the load-bearing claim (no longer trading on NYSE / now private) is confirmed at the primary source and cross-checked via WebSearch (Arconic portal, Paul Weiss, Glass Magazine all concur). Recommend optionally re-pointing url to the SEC primary or Arconic portal for a fully verbatim-fetchable source.
